short_description: Enveloped herpesvirus (human alphaherpesvirus 3, ~180-200 nm, pleomorphic) with the classic four-layer herpesvirus architecture: a ~125 kbp linear dsDNA genome packaged under pressure into a T=16 icosahedral capsid of 162 capsomeres (150 hexons + 12 pentons), the capsid cushioned by an asymmetric granular/fibrous protein tegument, the whole thing wrapped in a lipid envelope studded with short glycoprotein spikes (gB, gC, gE/gI, gH/gL, gK, gM/gN). Causes chickenpox on primary respiratory infection, then establishes lifelong latency in dorsal-root/cranial-nerve ganglia and can reactivate decades later as shingles (herpes zoster).

colour_legend.genome: coppery gold, tightly wound dsDNA fill inside the capsid
colour_legend.capsid: cool pale grey-blue icosahedral shell, 162 discrete capsomere facets visible
colour_legend.tegument: warm amber/tan granular padding filling the space between capsid and envelope - NOT a thin line, a substantial fibrous layer
colour_legend.envelope: soft translucent lilac-grey lipid bilayer, slightly irregular/scalloped outline (never a perfect circle)
colour_legend.glycoprotein_spikes: short blunt rose/pink studs evenly dotting the envelope surface - stubby, never long or rod-like
colour_legend.background: neutral dark charcoal (watercolour: warm aged cream paper)
colour_legend.note: A virion has no pigment of its own; electron micrographs (like the real PHIL 1878 TEM reference) image in greyscale, so every colour here is teaching convention. Keep this same structure->colour mapping across sem/textbook/3d/watercolor so the set reads as one poster.

do_not_draw: a naked capsid with no envelope - VZV is ALWAYS enveloped, unlike rotavirus/norovirus already in this atlas which are non-enveloped
a smooth, perfectly round, featureless envelope with no tegument between capsid and envelope - the tegument must read as a visible granular/fibrous layer filling real volume, not a thin membrane line
the tegument drawn as a second smooth membrane (it is amorphous/fibrous protein padding, not a lipid bilayer)
a helical, rod-shaped or filamentous capsid, or a bacteriophage head-and-tail body with tail fibres/base plate
long stalked club-shaped spikes (that is coronavirus/influenza) - VZV's glycoprotein spikes are short and blunt, densely packed studs, not long projections or rays
a perfectly spherical particle - the envelope is often slightly irregular / scalloped in outline, not a precise sphere (unlike many other enveloped viruses drawn too geometrically)
a segmented genome or RNA of any kind - the genome is a single linear DOUBLE-STRANDED DNA molecule, not RNA, not segmented, not a helix visible outside the capsid
bacterial features: cell wall, peptidoglycan, flagellum, pilus, capsule, nucleoid, ribosomes, mitochondria or any other cell organelle - a virion is not a cell

blisters, pustules, a rash, or any skin lesion depicted on a person in the four science styles (sem/textbook/3d/watercolor) - those are clinical signs of the disease, not virus morphology, and do not belong in these renders
a face, eyes, mouth or anthropomorphism on the virion in the four science styles (reserved for the separate kids' coloring page only)
any baked-in text, letters, numbers, labels, arrows, scale bars, rulers, legends or watermarks
a black border, dark frame, vignette, letterbox bar, mat, drop shadow, or the artwork drawn as a sheet/card lying on a surface

sources.claim: four-layer herpesvirus architecture (genome, T=16 icosahedral capsid of 162 capsomeres, tegument, glycoprotein-studded envelope); ~180-200 nm, pleomorphic; ~125 kbp linear dsDNA genome, smallest of the human herpesviruses; at least eight envelope glycoproteins (gB, gC, gE, gH, gI, gK, gL, gM/gN); latency in dorsal root/cranial/autonomic ganglia; reactivation as herpes zoster

sources.claim: real TEM reference shows a single isolated VZV virion with a bright electron-lucent-looking capsid core, granular tegument shell, and an irregular fuzzy envelope outline - i.e. the reference itself visually corroborates the four-layer architecture
sources.source: Direct visual inspection of CDC PHIL ID 1878 (see reference block below)

reference.native_pixel_size: lores JPEG 700 x 846 px (85,415 bytes, image/jpeg), verified via curl -sIL (HTTP 200) and Pillow; archival TIFF at https://phil.cdc.gov/PHIL_Images/1878/1878.tif is 3,204,474 bytes (HTTP 200, image/tiff) but was not downloaded
reference.verified: curl -sIL returned HTTP 200 (following the phil.cdc.gov -> wwwn.cdc.gov redirect); content-type image/jpeg, 85415 bytes; dimensions (700x846) confirmed by opening the downloaded file with Pillow. Visually verified by direct inspection: a single isolated VZV virion clearly showing a rounded lighter capsid core, a dark granular tegument shell around it, and an irregular, slightly scalloped outer envelope edge - textbook herpesvirus morphology, single specimen, no baked-in text or scale bar.
reference.note: fetch_reference.py center-crops the 700x846 source to 700x700 and upscales (Lanczos) to the standard 1080x1080 canvas - noting this explicitly as an upscale from native resolution, not additional real detail. No baked-in text or scale bar was present, so edit_image.py was intentionally skipped (per pipeline guidance: a plain deterministic crop/resize beats risking an image-editing model re-illustrating the texture).
